rows.source_label: Equation (1.1): q_t + A q_x = 0 for a constant real m by m matrix A
rows.next_foundation: Audit the existing real vector-field residual and classical solution definition against (1.1), without converting a definition into a circular solution theorem.

rows.source_label: The real scalar constant-coefficient equation is hyperbolic
Equation (1.2): q_t + ubar q_x = 0 for constant advection speed ubar
rows.next_foundation: Specialize the constant-coefficient residual to scalar advection.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.3): q(x,t) = qtilde(x - ubar t) solves the advection equation and propagates unchanged
Equation (1.4): w_t + c w_x = 0 with c positive models a right-going one-way wave
rows.next_foundation: Reuse the scalar-advection residual at positive speed and record the directional interpretation separately.

rows.source_label: Equations (1.2) and (1.4) are mathematically identical after renaming the unknown and speed
rows.next_foundation: Prove equality of the two residual specifications under the source renaming.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.5): p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0
rows.next_foundation: Audit the two classical acoustic constraints as a definition with explicit derivative and material conventions; rejected certificate projections do not dispose of definition coverage.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.6): q = (p,u) and A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]]
rows.next_foundation: Define the two-by-two acoustics matrix and prove componentwise equivalence with (1.5).

rows.source_label: For c = sqrt(K/rho), w1 = p + rho c u satisfies w1_t + c w1_x = 0
rows.next_foundation: Prove the right characteristic identity with explicit positivity and square-root hypotheses.

rows.source_label: w2 = p - rho c u satisfies w2_t - c w2_x = 0 and the printed left-going profile is q2(x,t) = qtilde(x+ct)
rows.next_foundation: Prove the left characteristic identity and formally adjudicate the printed q2 versus w2 notation mismatch.

rows.source_label: The two-equation acoustics system decomposes into two scalar waves moving in opposite directions
rows.next_foundation: Package the two characteristic maps as an invertible decomposition.

rows.source_label: A constant-coefficient system is hyperbolic when A has real eigenvalues and m linearly independent eigenvectors
Every vector in R^m decomposes uniquely as a linear combination of the eigenvectors
The eigenvalues of A give the speeds of the component waves
rows.next_foundation: Define eigenmode translated profiles and prove their speed-indexed residual identity.

rows.source_label: The acoustics matrix in (1.6) has eigenvalues -c and +c
rows.next_foundation: Exhibit and verify the two acoustics eigenpairs under K = rho c squared.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.7): differentiating (1.5) and eliminating mixed derivatives gives p_tt = c^2 p_xx
rows.next_foundation: Formalize second partial derivatives and the mixed-derivative elimination with explicit regularity.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.8): q_t + f(q)_x = 0 with flux function f
rows.next_foundation: Audit the existing scalar/system flux-divergence solution definition against (1.8), preserving the flux composition and implicit classical regularity.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.9): q_t + f'(q) q_x = 0 is the quasilinear form
rows.next_foundation: Prove the spatial chain-rule equivalence under differentiability of q and f.

rows.source_label: The quasilinear form suggests hyperbolicity when the flux Jacobian satisfies the matrix condition
rows.next_foundation: Define and audit the real complete-eigenbasis criterion for the actual flux Jacobian at each admissible state. Resolve pointwise versus stated-domain packaging; add neither strict hyperbolicity nor a well-posedness theorem.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.1) is a conservation law with linear flux f(q) = A q
rows.next_foundation: Prove the derivative of the linear flux and residual equality.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.10): for any two points x1 and x2, the time derivative of the interval integral is f(q(x1,t)) minus f(q(x2,t))
rows.next_foundation: Audit integral balance for arbitrary two endpoints, with incoming-minus-outgoing flux, and explicit time and integrability conventions.

rows.source_label: Contaminant mass conservation with flux f(q) = ubar q yields the advection equation
rows.next_foundation: Specialize the integral flux balance to the linear advection flux.

rows.source_label: Physical conservation of pressure and velocity is only approximate for very small disturbances in uniform media
rows.reason: This is the empirical small-disturbance modeling qualification. The separate ACOUSTICS-CONSERVATION-FORM row covers the exact algebraic assertion from the same paragraph.

rows.source_label: Sufficient smoothness of q and f(q) permits deriving (1.8) from the integral law (1.10)
rows.next_foundation: Formalize a fundamental-theorem-of-calculus bridge under explicit smoothness.

rows.source_label: Nonlinear conservation laws can develop discontinuities spontaneously from smooth initial data
rows.next_foundation: Extend the checked Burgers classical-breakdown prerequisite toward an explicit nonlinear conservation law with smooth initial data and an actual finite-time discontinuity in an admissible weak continuation. Gradient blow-up or absence of a global classical solution alone does not close this existential source claim.

rows.source_label: At a discontinuity the differential equation fails classically while the integral conservation law continues to hold
rows.next_foundation: Construct a moving-jump witness separating failure of classical spatial derivatives from valid time-integrated rectangle balance. Check the literal time derivative in (1.10) at endpoint crossings and obtain source/trace adjudication before choosing a faithful weak contract or certifying a discrepancy.

rows.source_label: A finite-volume unknown is the cell integral divided by cell volume rather than a point value
rows.next_foundation: Define one-dimensional cell averages on nondegenerate intervals.

rows.source_label: A time step modifies cell averages by edge fluxes computed from the available approximate averages
rows.next_foundation: Define a conservative one-step flux-difference update and prove telescoping conservation.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.11): Riemann initial data is q_l for x below zero and q_r for x above zero
rows.next_foundation: Audit the two-state piecewise initial-data definition with a free origin value. The general equation-plus-data definition is separately tracked by RIEMANN-INITIAL-VALUE-DEFINITION.

rows.source_label: Use neighboring cell averages as Riemann states to obtain numerical-flux and update information
rows.next_foundation: Define the interface-state adapter from adjacent cell averages.

rows.source_label: A hyperbolic Riemann solution is typically a function of x/t with finitely many constant-speed waves
rows.reason: The source explicitly qualifies this as typical and gives no theorem hypotheses, wave-count bound, admissibility condition, or nonlinear solution class.

rows.source_label: Solve linear hyperbolic Riemann data using eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A
rows.next_foundation: Search and audit an eigendata construction for linear hyperbolic Riemann data, preserving the unspecified value at the initial jump; construct missing foundations instead of skipping them.

rows.source_label: The simple wave structure extends to nonlinear systems with exact or arbitrarily accurate Riemann solutions constructible even for Euler
rows.reason: The broad exact-or-arbitrarily-accurate nonlinear construction claim fixes no system/domain, solver, error metric, admissibility class, existence hypotheses, or accuracy parameter. These missing truth conditions, rather than the later-chapter reference or a missing implementation, prevent a unique contract here.

rows.source_label: Shock or front tracking combines a smooth-region scheme with explicit discontinuity tracking and jump conditions
rows.reason: The paragraph only sketches a family of hybrid methods; it gives no front representation, smooth-region update, jump solver, time step, invariant, or correctness statement from which a checkable algorithm could be formalized.

rows.source_label: Shock capturing avoids explicit tracking, smears jumps over cells, and seeks correct jump conditions without nonphysical oscillations
rows.reason: The source describes a desired method class and qualitative behavior but specifies neither a numerical update nor definitions of smearing, correct jump conditions, or nonphysical oscillation.

rows.source_label: Use a normal Riemann solve at each two-dimensional edge or approximately planar three-dimensional face to determine flux
rows.reason: The chapter gives an implementation pattern without fixing a multidimensional mesh model, face orientation, normal-flux function, approximate Riemann solver, or update formula.

rows.source_label: On rectangular or logically rectangular grids, dimensional splitting solves one-dimensional coordinate-direction problems in turn
rows.next_foundation: Audit the existing ordered coordinate sweeps as function composition; preserve logically rectangular indexing and avoid attributing a fixed integrator or sweep order to Chapter 1.

rows.source_label: Assign heterogeneous material properties to each cell by averaging parameters over its volume
rows.next_foundation: Generalize the cell-average definition to material-parameter fields.

rows.source_label: Material-interface Riemann dynamics decomposes reflected and transmitted waves into neighboring cells
rows.reason: The reflected/transmitted-wave assertion omits the governing heterogeneous equations, interface conditions, wave families, and solver. The precise joint material/state initial-data construction is retained separately as MATERIAL-INTERFACE-RIEMANN-DATA; no wave-dynamics guarantee is inferred from that data definition.

rows.source_label: Wave-propagation methods use Riemann waves rather than interface fluxes, apply beyond conservation form, and connect to flux differencing on conservation laws
rows.reason: The asserted framework correspondence fixes no fluctuation operators, numerical interface update, applicability conditions, or equality relating wave propagation to flux differencing. These missing operators and hypotheses prevent a checkable mathematical correspondence in this passage.

rows.source_label: q denotes the PDE solution while u is reserved for velocity or the x component of (u,v)
rows.reason: Editorial choice of names for the solution and physical velocity; the equation roles are inventoried separately.

rows.source_label: Q_i^n and Q_ij^n denote numerical approximations; subscripts are spatial and n is the time level
rows.reason: Editorial subscript/superscript convention for cell and time indices. Mathematical arrays, averaging and current-step dependence have separate inventory coverage.

rows.source_label: For m equations q and Q are m-vectors and q^p denotes component p
rows.reason: Editorial notation for components of the m-dimensional state and numerical array. Dimension and field shape are covered by the system and finite-volume definitions.

rows.source_label: Superscripts enumerate eigenvalues lambda^p and eigenvectors r^p
rows.reason: Editorial superscript convention for a finite eigenfamily; the mathematical eigenbasis content is separately inventoried.

rows.source_label: Initial data is denoted by a circle over the variable
rows.reason: The circle accent is purely a printed convention for initial data and contributes no proposition or reusable mathematical definition.

rows.source_label: psi and p are deliberately overloaded in separated contexts
rows.reason: The passage is an editorial warning about context-dependent printed symbols, not a claim suitable for a Lean declaration.

rows.source_label: The q-Riemann symbol denotes the similarity-solution value along x/t = 0 for data q_l and q_r
rows.next_foundation: Audit evaluation along ray zero for a selected similarity solution, recording any needed trace convention without imposing uniqueness absent from the source.

rows.source_label: The constant-coefficient linear acoustics equations have conservation form for pressure and velocity
rows.next_foundation: Reuse and independently audit the integrated acoustics conservation-form wrapper and its linear-flux producer.

rows.source_label: Equation (1.7) is hyperbolic under the standard classification of second-order linear equations
rows.next_foundation: Identify a source-compatible principal-part classification for the positive-speed wave equation and search current project and Mathlib producers.

rows.source_label: In a one-step method the solution at the next time level is determined entirely by data at the current time level
rows.next_foundation: Audit a transition-map representation with current-time input and next-time output; keep typography separate from the defining dependence.

rows.source_label: If contaminant mass is not conserved, the conservation law must contain source terms
rows.next_foundation: Place and audit the checked mass-budget defect/source-integral bridge, specialize to contaminant transport, and exhibit a nonzero internal-production example. A nonzero mass derivative alone is insufficient because endpoint transport must first be subtracted.

rows.source_label: Shock waves can only appear from nonlinear phenomena in the surrounding discussion of initially smooth small-amplitude waves
rows.reason: The physical slogan leaves formation versus prescribed discontinuity, the shock/admissibility class, coefficient regularity, initial/boundary data, solution concept, and time quantifiers unspecified. These affect truth conditions: linear Riemann data already permits jumps. Smoothness preservation for constant-coefficient evolution is only a specified subcase, not coverage of the unrestricted slogan.

rows.source_label: The finite-volume high-resolution methods discussed are typically at best second-order accurate
rows.reason: The qualified assertion fixes no method/reconstruction/limiter/time-integrator class, error norm, local versus global or spatial versus temporal order, data regularity, mesh/time relation, quantification of typical, or non-improvability bound for at best. An O(h^2) upper bound or one selected scheme does not establish this unspecified method-class claim.

rows.source_label: Hyperbolic equations with variable coefficients may not be in conservation form
rows.next_foundation: Strengthen the checked state-only flux obstruction with the positive smooth coefficient 1+x^2 and a calculus bridge from arbitrary smooth test fields. Preserve the density q, and resolve whether explicit spatial fluxes are included; do not claim absence of conservative reformulations after changing density.

rows.source_label: Every constant real hyperbolic system decouples in an eigenbasis into scalar advection equations, with reconstruction of the state
rows.next_foundation: Place and independently audit the checked arbitrary-field PDE equivalence under a fixed real eigenbasis and its reconstruction identity. Keep repeated eigenvalues admissible; a constructed eigenmode family alone is insufficient.

rows.source_label: Material-interface Riemann initial data prescribes jumps in both medium and state at x=0
rows.next_foundation: Define paired material/state Riemann data for arbitrary material and state types with a free origin value, then verify its left/right projections and audit the source correspondence separately from reflected/transmitted-wave dynamics.

rows.source_label: Riemann initial-value configuration: a hyperbolic equation together with piecewise constant two-state initial data
rows.next_foundation: Represent an independently supplied hyperbolic equation/solution predicate together with the two-state initial-data condition. Preserve the unspecified origin value and avoid restricting this general definition to constant matrices.
